From Skill to Self-Reliance
articles.full_content:
Smt. Shalaka Nagotkar's Entrepreneurial Journey
Professional skills can create meaningful livelihood opportunities when supported by timely and affordable finance. Institutional assistance enables aspiring entrepreneurs to overcome initial financial barriers, establish sustainable enterprises and move towards economic independence.
Smt. Shalaka Darshan Nagotkar, a graduate and trained beauty professional from Kalyan (West), Thane, Maharashtra, established a home-based beauty parlour with financial assistance of Rs. 3,75,000 under the NSFDC Term Loan Scheme. Today, she earns a monthly net income of approximately Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000 and supports her family through her enterprise.
Smt. Shalaka holds a diploma in Beauty Parlour and aspired to use her professional skills to become financially independent. However, she did not own a shop, and the high rent of commercial premises made it difficult for her to start a business.
After learning about NSFDC schemes through the internet, she approached the Thane Branch of the Leather Industries Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited (LIDCOM). She received financial assistance of Rs. 3,75,000 under the NSFDC Term Loan Scheme. The loan was disbursed on 30 October 2024 to help her establish her own beauty parlour.
To manage the high cost of commercial space, Smt. Shalaka made a practical beginning by operating the beauty parlour from her home in Kalyan (West). The assistance enabled her to purchase the equipment and materials required to provide professional beauty and grooming services.
Through her skills, dedication and consistent efforts, she developed a stable source of livelihood. Her beauty parlour now provides her with a monthly net income of approximately Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000, strengthening her financial independence and helping her support her family.
Smt. Shalaka has expressed her gratitude to NSFDC for the financial assistance provided under the Term Loan Scheme. Her journey demonstrates how professional skills, determination and timely credit support can enable women entrepreneurs to build sustainable livelihoods and become self-reliant.
SS-88-TAR-KV-GA-RK

NSC Approves ₹320 Crore under PM-SETU for Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana; Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited to Partner in Transformation of Seven ITIs
articles.full_content:
Cumulative PM-SETU investment now reaches ₹2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, advancing the creation of modern, industry-led and future-ready vocational training institutions nationwide Bringing Industry Closer to ITIs Will Create Stronger Employment Pathways for Youth: Jayant Chaudhary
The National Steering Committee (NSC) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has approved a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) worth ₹320 crore for the Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme. Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited will partner with the Government of Haryana as the Anchor Industry Partner for the cluster.
With this approval, the cumulative investment sanctioned under PM-SETU has risen to ₹2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to transforming Industrial Training Institutes into industry-led, future-ready centres of excellence that are aligned with evolving workforce requirements.
The approval marks another significant step towards strengthening the industry-led transformation of Government Industrial Training Institutes and creating a more demand-driven vocational training ecosystem.
Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said: "Bringing industry closer to ITIs will create stronger employment pathways for our youth. The approval of the Kurukshetra cluster under PM-SETU reflects our commitment to making skill development more relevant, aspirational and responsive to the changing needs of industry. Through strong industry partnerships, we are working to ensure that young people are equipped with the skills, exposure and opportunities required to participate meaningfully in India's growth story”.
One Hub and Six Spoke ITIs to be Transformed
The Kurukshetra cluster will be developed under the Hub-and-Spoke model envisaged under PM-SETU and will comprise seven Government ITIs.
Government ITI, Kurukshetra will serve as the Hub ITI, while the following institutes will function as Spoke ITIs:
• Government ITI (Women), Kurukshetra
• Government ITI, Kaithal
• Government ITI (Women), Kaithal
• Government ITI, Pehowa
• Government ITI, Pabnawa
• Government ITI (Women), Ambala City
The ₹320 crore investment will support the development of an integrated and industry-responsive skilling ecosystem across the cluster. The proposed interventions will focus on strengthening infrastructure, modernising training facilities, introducing industry-aligned courses, and enhancing employability outcomes for trainees.
Strengthening Industry-ITI Linkages
Under PM-SETU, industry partners play a central role in shaping the transformation of ITIs through curriculum development, infrastructure enhancement, training delivery, faculty engagement, apprenticeships, industry exposure and placement support. Ministry of MSME Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 on Swachhata and Disposal of Pendency
articles.full_content:
Ministry has disposed 22,365 Public Grievances and Freed 1,167 Sq. Ft. Space under Special Campaign 5.0
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) is gearing up for Special Campaign 6.0, to be conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026 under the aegis of the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign seeks to improve cleanliness and citizen experience across Government offices, with this edition placing added emphasis on “effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” in line with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, and on field/outstation offices that directly interface with the public, besides Ministries/Departments, their attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and PSUs.
A Preparatory Phase (15–30 September, 2026) is currently underway, during which the Ministry is sensitizing offices down to the field level, and drawing up an action plan for the campaign. The subsequent Implementation Phase (2–31 October, 2026) will drive cleanliness, e-waste disposal, digitisation, record weeding, space management, and clearance of pending MP References, State Government references, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, and public grievances.
In Special Campaign 5.0, the Ministry and its organisations — the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi & Village Industries Commission, Coir Board, National Small Industries Corporation, National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, and Mahatma Gandhi Institute for Rural Industrialisation — reviewed 23,162 physical files, weeded out 4,280 files, freed up 21,045 sq. ft. of office space, and disposed of scrap worth ₹22.89 lakh. Over 81% of MP references and 99% of public grievances were cleared, as part of 1,045 cleanliness campaigns conducted during the period.
Further, pursuant to DARPG’s directions to sustain the momentum generated under Special Campaign 5.0, Ministry directed its organisations to undertake activities on various parameters of the Campaign. As a result, during the period from November, 2025 to September 2026, 22,365 Public Grievances, 4850 Public Grievances Appeals, 226 MP references have been disposed; 626 Physical files and 127 E-files have been weeded out after review and around 1167 sq ft. of space has been freed. Moreover, officers of the Ministry have visited its field offices and institutions, to sensitise the staff, and review their performance in the Campaign.
Sensitization workshop at NSIC Branch Office Guwahati
Plantation drive at DFO-Branch officer, Aurangabad
Building on these gains, the Ministry and its organisations remain committed to carry Special Campaign 6.0 forward with the same rigour, towards cleaner and more responsive governance.
Sunil Kumar Tiwari

Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited will continue to play a central role towards achievement of India’s clean energy vision: Shri Shripad Yesso Naik
articles.full_content:
SECI celebrates its 15th Foundation Day with Stakeholders’ Meet
“SECI's 15-year journey stands as a reflection of India's growing leadership in the global renewable energy transition,” said Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy and Power while addressing the gathering at the celebration of the 15th Foundation Day of Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) here today as the Chief Guest.
Shri Naik said that SECI has consistently delivered on the nation’s clean energy vision and expressed confidence that the corporation will continue to play a central role towards its achievement.
The event was also graced by Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE and Shri Vivek Jain, Chairman, INOXGFL Group along with other senior officials of the Renewable Energy sector.
Speaking at the event, Shri Akash Tripathi, Managing Director, SECI, said that SECI remains committed to open new opportunities in the renewable energy sector, working closely with all stakeholders and innovating with market's requirements. These 15 years have been a testament to SECI's dedication and the nation's collective will towards sustainable energy. We are thankful to all our stakeholders for putting their faith in us.
The Stakeholders’ Meet featured two thematic sessions, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules” and “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” bringing together policymakers, industry leaders and financial institutions to deliberate on emerging opportunities and challenges shaping India’s energy transition.
The first session, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules,” explored the role of green hydrogen and its derivatives in decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors and creating new avenues for industrial growth. The session covered opportunities for domestic production and emerging applications, along with the policy support, infrastructure, technology and financing required to develop green molecule markets on a scale.
The second session, “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” examined the evolving role of distributed RE in India. Key areas of discussion included greater consumer participation, integration of distributed energy resources and emerging market mechanisms, as well as the policy and regulatory frameworks needed to facilitate their effective integration and support the expansion of renewable energy.
As SECI marks 15 years of service to the nation, its cumulative achievements stand at over 41 GW of renewable energy generation capacity commissioned through third-party developers, power sale agreements of over 67 GW signed with various DISCOMs/consumers, and cumulative market investments enabled for about ₹3.6 lakh crores. The company is rapidly scaling with its own projects' portfolio as well and is also active in promoting energy storage, green hydrogen and allied areas.

"BPCL’s commitment to skill development commendable" - Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary at SDI Kochi
articles.full_content:
Kochi, 19 September 2026: “BPCL’s decade-long commitment to skill development through SDI Kochi is commendable. What impressed me most is the focus on inclusive skilling and industry-aligned, future-ready training that truly empowers our youth,”* said Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, during his visit to Skill Development Institute (SDI), Kochi today.
Shri Chaudhary was accompanied by Shri Sujith Kumar, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship. He was welcomed by Shri Chacko M. Jose, Executive Director (Kochi Refinery) & Director (Refinery), BPCL - Designate, Shri Meganathan, GM (HR), BPCL, Shri Sivakumar G.S., CEO, SDI Kochi, and senior representatives from BPCL and the Central and State skill development ecosystem.
Established in 2016 by Skill Development Society, Kochi, chaired by BPCL, SDI Kochi is a flagship CSR initiative of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. The institute has certified around 2,100 dipla holders to date, achieving an impressive *98% placement record. SDI Kochi offers a six-month fully residential program at a nominal fee of only Rs. 5,000/-, making quality skill training accessible to youth from economically weaker sections. Courses offered include: Industrial Electrician, Industrial Welder, Electronic Manufacturing, Fitter Fabrication, and Process Instrument Operator – all designed to meet current industry demands. A key highlight of the visit was the Minister’s interaction with hearing-impaired trainees, where he appreciated their confidence and commitment, underlining the importance of inclusive skilling for self-reliance. The Minister lauded the SDI model and called for stronger collaboration between Government, industry and skill institutions to build a skilled and Atmanirbhar Bharat

Unemployment Rate Reduced from 6% to 3.2% Due to Government’s Flagship Schemes: Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of State Dr. L. Murugan Distributes Appointment Letters to 285 Newly Recruited Candidates at 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated through video conferencing in the 20th Rozgar Mela, organised at 45 locations across the country, and distributed appointment letters to more than 51,000 newly recruited youth.
Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, participated in the Rozgar Mela held at D.G. Vaishnav College, Chennai. He distributed appointment letters to 285 newly recruited candidates selected for various Central Government Ministries, Departments, and organisations, extending his best wishes to youngsters joining key bodies including the Income Tax Department, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Airports Authority of India, Ministry of Defence, Department of Posts, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), and Southern Railway.
Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan said that the newly recruited youth entering Government service would play an important role in achieving the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged the recruits to view their responsibilities not merely as securing employment, but as an opportunity to serve the nation and contribute to its holistic development.
He stated that an appointment letter is not merely an order of appointment but an opportunity to serve the nation, noting that Government employees function as representatives and the face of the Government while interacting with citizens. He emphasised that honesty, accountability, empathy, and a humane approach towards the public should remain integral to public service.
The Union Minister highlighted that various flagship initiatives of the Government, including Make in India, Start-up India, Stand-up India, and the MUDRA loan scheme, have enabled the youth to emerge as job creators in addition to being job seekers. He stated that the unemployment rate has declined from 6 per cent to 3.2 per cent as a result of various initiatives undertaken by the Government.
Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan pointed out that the number of startups in the country, which stood at around 400 in 2014, has increased to more than 2.5 lakh, noting that a significant number of startup founders are youth below the age of 30.
He also underscored the importance of continuous learning, adoption of new technologies, and regular upgradation of professional skills. He highlighted the growing opportunities for youth in frontier sectors such as space technology and atomic energy, while noting the increasing participation of women across sectors, including space, defence, education, governance, and public administration.
The Union Minister added that more than 12.75 lakh appointment letters have been distributed through Rozgar Melas so far, reflecting the Government’s dedicated emphasis on creating employment opportunities for the youth.

The two-day Education Conclave 2026 on “Implementation of NEP 2020: Vision, Challenges & Opportunities for the North Eastern States” concluded here on Saturday with a call for stronger regional cooperation, skill development, research and industry-academia linkages.
articles.full_content:
Tripura Higher Education Minister Kishor Barman, addressing the valedictory session, said the success of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 would depend on effective implementation and tangible improvements in the lives of students, particularly those in remote areas.
He said education should move beyond degree-oriented learning and equip students with skills, critical thinking, creativity, entrepreneurship and adaptability. He called for greater emphasis on internships, apprenticeships, incubation and entrepreneurship programmes to enable students to become job creators.
Barman also proposed greater collaboration among Northeastern states through faculty networks, shared research infrastructure, student mobility and joint research projects. He identified five key areas emerging from the conclave—access, quality, skills, research and innovation, and entrepreneurship.
Additional Secretary, Higher and Technical Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India, Anandrao V. Patel, stressed the need to integrate skills, industry exposure and multidisciplinary education into NEP implementation.
Patel highlighted the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme and said industry-academia collaboration was essential to prepare students for changing workplace requirements. He also called for greater student mobility across the Northeast through multiple entry and exit, credit transfer and the Academic Bank of Credits.
He said achieving the target of 50% Gross Enrolment Ratio by 2035 would require additional infrastructure, teachers and teacher training, along with coordinated efforts by states.
Patel further highlighted online and open-distance learning, multilingual education, virtual laboratories and digital platforms such as SWAYAM and SWAYAM Plus as important tools for expanding access to education.
The conclave resolutions and outcomes were presented by the officer-in-charge of the Documentation Committee. The session, chaired by V. Lovitoly Sema, Additional Secretary, Higher & Technical Education and Director, Higher Education, Government of Nagaland, concluded with a vote of thanks by Tiakaba Amer, Additional Director, Technical Education, followed by the national anthem.
